Native American tribes who have lived inside the boundaries of present-day Texas include the ___E:Alabama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_people)___ , ___E:Apache U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apache)___ , ___E:Atakapan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atakapa)___ , ___E:Bidai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bidai)___ , ___E:Caddo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caddo)___ , ___E:Aranama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranama_people)___ , ___E:Comanche U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comanche)___ , ___E:Choctaw U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choctaw)___ , ___E:Coushatta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coushatta)___ , ___E:Hasinai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasinai)___ , ___E:Jumano U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jumano_people)___ , ___E:Karankawa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karankawa_people)___ , ___E:Kickapoo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kickapoo_people)___ , ___E:Kiowa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiowa)___ , ___E:Tonkawa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonkawa)___ , and ___E:Wichita U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita_people)___ .

In 1690 Spanish authorities, concerned that France posed a competitive threat, constructed several ___E:missions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_missions_in_Texas)___ in ___E:East Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Texas)___ among the Caddo.

Hoping more settlers would reduce the near-constant Comanche raids, ___E:Mexican Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Texas)___ liberalized its immigration policies to permit immigrants from outside Mexico and Spain.
As a result of this, large swathes of land were allotted to empresarios , who recruited settlers from the United States, Europe, and the Mexican interior, primarily the U.S.

The ___E:Anahuac Disturbances U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anahuac_Disturbances)___ in 1832 were the first open revolt against Mexican rule, coinciding with a revolt in Mexico against the nation's president.  ___E:Texians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texian)___ sided with the ___E:federalists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federalism)___ against the government and drove all Mexican soldiers out of East Texas.

The following year, Texians reiterated their demands at the ___E:Convention of 1833 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convention_of_1833)___ .
Within Mexico, tensions continued between federalists and centralists.
In early 1835, wary ___E:Texians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texians)___ formed Committees of Correspondence and Safety.
The unrest erupted into armed conflict in late 1835 at the ___E:Battle of Gonzales U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Gonzales)___ .
This launched the ___E:Texas Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Revolution)___ .
Texians elected delegates to the ___E:Consultation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consultation_(Texas))___ , which created a provisional government.
The provisional government soon collapsed from infighting, and Texas was without clear governance for the first two months of 1836.
Mexican President ___E:Antonio López de Santa Anna U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_L%C3%B3pez_de_Santa_Anna)___ personally led an army to end the revolt.

General ___E:José de Urrea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_de_Urrea)___ defeated all the Texian resistance along the coast culminating in the ___E:Goliad massacre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goliad_massacre)___ .

López de Santa Anna's forces, after a ___E:thirteen-day siege U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_the_Alamo)___ , overwhelmed Texian defenders at the ___E:Battle of the Alamo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Alamo)___ .
News of the defeats sparked panic among Texas settlers.

The newly elected Texian delegates to the ___E:Convention of 1836 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convention_of_1836)___ quickly signed a ___E:declaration of independence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Declaration_of_Independence)___ on March 2, forming the ___E:Republic of Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Texas)___ .

Texas has ___E:254 counties U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_counties_in_Texas)___ , more than any other state.

Each county runs on ___E:Commissioners' Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commissioners%27_Court)___ system consisting of four elected commissioners (one from each of four precincts in the county, roughly divided according to population) and a county judge elected at large from the entire county.

County government runs similar to a "weak" ___E:mayor-council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor-council)___ system; the county judge has no veto authority, but votes along with the other commissioners.

Although Texas permits cities and counties to enter "interlocal agreements" to share services, the state does not allow ___E:consolidated city-county U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consolidated_city-county)___ governments, nor does it have ___E:metropolitan governments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_government)___ .

Counties are not granted ___E:home rule U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_rule)___ status; their powers are strictly defined by state law.   The state does not have townships—areas within a county are either incorporated or unincorporated.
Incorporated areas are part of a municipality.
The county provides limited services to unincorporated areas and to some smaller incorporated areas.
Municipalities are classified either "general law" cities or "home rule".
A municipality may elect home rule status once it exceeds 5,000 population with voter approval.
Texas also permits the creation of "special districts", which provide limited services.
The most common is the ___E:school district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_district)___ , but can also include hospital districts, community college districts, and utility districts.

Municipal, school district, and special district elections are ___E:nonpartisan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-partisan_democracy)___ ,  though the party affiliation of a candidate may be well-known.
County and state elections are partisan.
